items.text: Anyone willing to work and obey the law should be free to settle in whatever country they choose.
items.rationale: Open-borders view held by libertarians, left internationalists and some religious universalists; the obey-the-law clause stops it being a strawman. Ideal vs here-and-now splits are likely (principled support, practical doubts).

items.text: Large numbers of immigrants should be welcomed each year.
items.rationale: Plain pro-immigration lean (liberals, pro-growth business conservatives, progressives); an absolute level rather than a comparison with today, so it reads the same in both frames.

items.text: If people are fleeing war or persecution, they should be taken in, even in large numbers.
items.rationale: Humanitarian and religious-charity view; the condition favours Pluralist and 'even in large numbers' keeps it polar. Assumes the refugee situation in whichever frame is judged; capacity worries may split the frames.

items.text: Newcomers should be able to keep their own way of life without being pressed to fit in with the majority.
items.rationale: Core multiculturalist and liberal-pluralist position; mirrors mul-11. 'Without being pressed' is the polar claim, not a negation of an existing affirmative. Works in both frames.

items.text: All cultures present in a country should have equal standing in public life.
items.rationale: Strong multiculturalism (no favoured majority culture); also held by plurinational and polycentric traditions. Mirrors mul-12. Reads cleanly as an ideal and as a judgement of one's own country.

items.text: If a minority community wants schools that teach in its own language and traditions, that should be supported.
items.rationale: Communal-autonomy view held by multiculturalists, religious-minority advocates and some communitarians; the condition favours Pluralist. Mirrors mul-14. Agent-neutral 'supported' fits state, community or voluntary provision.

items.text: If many residents speak a minority language, public services should be offered in that language.
items.rationale: Linguistic-pluralism view (multilingual states, minority-rights advocates); the condition favours Pluralist. Assimilationists who favour one common language will disagree. Meaningful in both frames.

items.text: Newcomers should be admitted only when it clearly benefits the people already living there.
items.rationale: Strong restrictionist position (national conservatives, some labour-protection left); framed as a principle of selection, not hostility, so adherents recognise it. Matches mul-01 in strength.

items.text: Only small numbers of immigrants should be admitted each year.
items.rationale: Plain low-immigration lean; the direct mirror of mul-02 at the same level. Absolute level, not relative to today, so both frames read naturally.

items.text: If housing or jobs are scarce, immigration should be held to very low levels.
items.rationale: Scarcity-based restriction argued by nationalists, some trade unionists and environmental-limits advocates; the condition favours Assimilationist. Mirrors mul-03. Assumes scarcity in whichever frame is judged.

items.text: Newcomers should be expected to take on the way of life of the country they join.
items.rationale: Core assimilationist expectation (civic republicans, cultural conservatives); mirrors mul-04. Says 'expected' rather than 'forced' to stay at level 2. Works in both frames.

items.text: A country should have one shared culture that everyone living there is expected to adopt.
items.rationale: Strong common-culture view held by civic-republican unitarists and cultural nationalists alike; mirrors mul-05. Not a caricature: it names a shared culture, not an ethnicity.

items.text: If a group's customs clash with the majority's way of life, the group should be the one to adapt.
items.rationale: Host-culture-precedence view; the condition (a real clash) favours Assimilationist. Pluralists expect mutual accommodation and will disagree. Works in both frames.

items.text: If newcomers set up separate schools to keep their own culture, that should be discouraged in favor of common schools.
items.rationale: Common-school and anti-'parallel society' view held by civic republicans and secular integrationists; mirrors mul-06. The condition favours Assimilationist. 'Discouraged' (not banned) keeps it at level 2.
